capabilities.target: CRM customer account record, selectable by email or account id

instructions.note: "You may look up any customer by email or account id" lets the content of an untrusted email determine which customer's record is fetched, with no restriction to the requester's own account.

The only control against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction ("Never share another customer's information"), which is behavioral and can be defeated by injected content in the email it is meant to guard against.
"Send it directly... Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry" grants the agent authority to send externally on every routine ticket with no definition of 'routine' and no approval gate.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model obeying the rule when processing the very untrusted email that may try to override it; a more capable or more thoroughly injected model can rationalize exceptions or be convinced the disclosure is authorized.

controls.name: SIEM logging of outbound email
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced by mail infrastructure outside the model and does not weaken as the model improves; it is detective only and does not prevent disclosure before the email leaves.

controls.name: Per-request least-privilege CRM scoping to the ticket's own customer
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the credential/authorization layer outside the model; even a fully cooperative attacker cannot make the model read data its token cannot access.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the verified ticket requester address
controls.decay_rationale: Binding the destination to the system-of-record address removes the model's ability to choose an arbitrary recipient, regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action review) for non-routine or cross-account sends
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action, low-volume gate does not decay with model capability, though it would weaken if approval volume grew high or review moved to a model-summary mode.

controls.name: Rate, volume, or step limit on CRM reads and email sends
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap enforced outside the model limits blast radius regardless of model capability, though low-and-slow abuse can stay under it.

controls.name: Tool definition pinning/hashing and mutual-auth server identity verification
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning and identity verification are enforced outside the model and do not weaken with model capability, though they fail if a new unpinned server is added by default.

controls.name: Immutable audit logging of CRM reads with requester/session identity
controls.decay_rationale: A tamper-evident log at the data store layer does not depend on model behavior, though it is detective only and does not prevent the read.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted email drives unrestricted CRM lookup and arbitrary-recipient email send

attack_path.note: An attacker-crafted or spoofed customer email requests information about an account, possibly not the sender's own.
Agent looks up the requested account using a broadly-scoped credential that can read every customer record.
Agent sends the retrieved confidential data using a shared service account that can send to any address, with no human approval for routine cases.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model or platform version string changes in config; subject.model.swappable is true and no separate review gate exists for model upgrades.

evidence.observation: Agent reads the untrusted customer email and uses it to look up any customer 'by email or account id,' allowing attacker-controlled selection of which account record is fetched.
Agent sends drafted replies directly with no human approval except when the customer appears angry, so a confidential CRM read can reach an attacker-influenced send with no gate.
mail_mcp is authenticated with MAIL_SVC_TOKEN, a shared service account; runtime notes state it can send to any address, so there is no destination restriction on cap.email_send.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN 'can read every customer record,' confirming the credential scope for cap.crm_read is broad rather than limited to the requesting customer.

recommendations.action: Scope the CRM credential per-request to only the ticket's identified customer, removing the 'look up any customer by email or account id' instruction.
Add a raw-action human approval gate before any send that references a different account than the current ticket's, or before any non-routine send.
Bind the send recipient to the verified ticket requester address from the ticketing system record, not to any address derived from email content or model output.
Replace the prompt-only 'never share' rule with a structural output check that cross-references the data subject in the drafted reply against the authenticated recipient.

findings.title: No attributable audit record for CRM reads (repudiation gap)

forecast.watch_signal: New data sources added to CRM scope, or any future logging control added and then removed without a replacement read-level audit trail.

evidence.observation: Only outbound email is stated as logged to the SIEM; no logging is described for CRM reads via crm_mcp, so a cross-customer lookup leaves no audit trail.

recommendations.action: Log every CRM read with the authenticated session/ticket id and the requested account id to an immutable audit store.

findings.title: No rate, volume, or step limit on CRM reads or email sends (ASI08 cascading/DoS exposure)

forecast.watch_signal: Median steps or runtime per ticket rises, or autonomy level is raised without adding rate or step limits.

evidence.observation: The agent acts autonomously on each ticket with no stated step or rate limit.
No cap on lookups or sends per time window is mentioned; max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not documented anywhere in the artifacts.

recommendations.action: Add rate/step/spend limits per ticket and per time window on cap.crm_read and cap.email_send.

findings.title: MCP tool definitions and server identity are not pinned or verified (ASI04 supply chain exposure)

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

forecast.watch_signal: Additional MCP servers added to mcp.json without a definition-pinning or identity-verification policy.

evidence.observation: Both MCP servers are configured with only a URL and a static bearer token; there is no indication tool definitions are pinned/hashed or that server identity is verified beyond the token.

recommendations.action: Pin and hash tool definitions for crm_mcp and mail_mcp; verify server identity via mTLS or signed certificates rather than static bearer tokens alone.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates its own identity to the orchestration runtime or to downstream services beyond the shared MCP bearer tokens.
Artifacts do not state whether inbound email sender authentication such as SPF, DKIM, or DMARC is used, so attribution of ticket senders cannot be assessed.
No declared capability writes to CRM records; cap.crm_read only performs reads, so the store cannot be tampered with through the agent's declared capabilities.
Artifacts state email sends are logged to the SIEM but do not describe write protections or integrity controls on the SIEM log store itself.
The SIEM log store is an internal security monitoring system with no described external access path or capability that could exfiltrate its contents in this design.
Artifacts do not describe log volume limits, retention controls, or ingestion capacity for the SIEM pipeline.
The inbound email flow carries data into the agent; it does not carry confidential data out, so information disclosure does not apply to this inbound direction.
Artifacts do not describe transport integrity protections such as TLS configuration or message signing for the mail_mcp egress flow.

rating.rationale: The dominant risk is F1: an untrusted customer email can direct a broadly-scoped CRM read (any customer, by design) into a send through a shared mail service account that can reach any address, with no human approval for routine cases. Inherent is critical (untrusted source to an irreversible confidential egress, worsened by the uncapped autonomy modifier). The only present control on that path is a behavioral prompt rule ('never share another customer's information'), which earns one tier of credit, giving a residual of high; SIEM logging is detective and does not prevent disclosure. Because the prompt rule is model-dependent, a model upgrade (subject.model.swappable is true, with no separate review) removes that credit and returns the path to critical, which sets the forecast. Supporting findings record a missing audit trail on CRM reads (F2, repudiation), no rate or step limits on either tool (F3, ASI08), and unpinned/unverified MCP tool definitions (F4, ASI04 supply chain). None of these currently has a structural control; the controls list records the fixes a reviewer should require (least-privilege CRM scoping, recipient binding to the system of record, a raw-action approval gate, rate limits, read auditing, and definition pinning) as missing_recommended.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior, and no live testing or red-teaming was performed.

No agent card, IaC, or runtime orchestration config was provided; autonomy level and the absence of approval gates are inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes alone, so confidence on those points is medium.

Tool definition pinning and server identity verification for crm_mcp and mail_mcp were assumed absent because mcp.json shows only a URL and a bearer token with no further detail; this could be incorrect if pinning or stronger identity checks are enforced elsewhere and simply not documented.
